findings.statement: Scope: the run run:5ce89f521e5e is a bounded replay (not cancelled, clink exit status 0, 3 of 3 jobs completed) of 50,000 events. It holds 50,000 transfers, 12,072 accounts, 12,321 devices, 691 onward links and 6 fan-in alerts. Fan-in means at least 5 distinct senders inside one event-time hour. An onward link means a debit within 1,800,000 ms (30 min) after a credit. Everything below holds only for this dataset as this run processed it.

Alert fan_in:A-37573:1794823200000. Window 1794823200000 to 1794826800000; 7 senders, 7 transfers, total 379500. All 7 contributing transfers start onward links. T003057, T003091, T003124 and T003154 link to T003168. T003248, T003287 and T003319 link to T003391. This gives two separate 4-link sequences through the same accounts, A-37573 > A-38045 > A-93288 > A-63022 > A-54215. Both end at A-54215, which sent no transfers in this dataset. Max depth is 4. Path accounts: A-37573, A-38045, A-93288, A-63022, A-54215.

Alert fan_in:A-37573:1794823200000, devices: all 8 onward transfers on its paths were sent from one device, D-45880. In this dataset D-45880 was used by exactly four accounts, A-37573, A-38045, A-93288 and A-63022, all of them on this alert's paths.

Alert fan_in:A-85921:1794855600000. Window 1794855600000 to 1794859200000; 6 senders, 6 transfers, total 15000. Every contributing transfer is 2500. T005750, T005789, T005830 and T005868 link to T005888 (A-85921 to A-10758, 9500). A-10758 sent nothing in this dataset, so the paths end there. T005934 and T005978 arrived after T005888 and have no onward link. Max depth is 1. Path accounts: A-85921, A-10758. No device was used by two or more of its path accounts.

Alert fan_in:A-10859:1794924000000. Window 1794924000000 to 1794927600000; 6 senders, 6 transfers, total 204000. All 6 contributing transfers start onward links. Paths go from A-10859 to A-78340 (via T011583 or T011670). From A-78340 they either go A-75793 > A-92332 (T011600, T011628; 3 links) or end at A-85287 (T011695; 2 links). Max depth is 3. The paths end at two accounts, A-92332 and A-85287. Path accounts: A-10859, A-78340, A-75793, A-92332, A-85287. Device D-79802 was used by A-10859 and A-78340, the alerted account and the first account after it. It was used by no other account in the dataset.

Alert fan_in:A-28137:1795003200000. Window 1795003200000 to 1795006800000; 7 senders, 7 transfers, total 29500. None of its 7 contributing transfers has an onward link, so it has no onward paths: max depth 0, no end accounts, and its only path account is A-28137. A-28137's only debit in the dataset is T018852 (21000, to A-87539, at 1795013700000). That is 7,440,000 ms after its last contributing credit (T018248), beyond the 30-minute onward window, and no onward link points to it. No shared device on its path.

Alert fan_in:A-83577:1795057200000. Window 1795057200000 to 1795060800000; 8 senders, 8 transfers, total 174500. All 8 contributing transfers link to T022572. From there one 5-link sequence runs A-83577 > A-56768 > A-83094 > A-43725 > A-14799 > A-39382, the deepest path of any alert. It ends at A-39382, which sent nothing in this dataset. Path accounts: A-83577, A-56768, A-83094, A-43725, A-14799, A-39382.

Alert fan_in:A-83577:1795057200000, devices: D-40018 was used by two of its path accounts, A-83094 (T022609) and A-14799 (T022649). These are not adjacent on the path. D-40018 was also used by A-34114, which is not on any alert path, for T038409 (12000 to A-39862 at 1795252440000). T038409 has no onward links. The other path transfers each used a device that only that account used among those listed.

Alert fan_in:A-20636:1795190400000. Window 1795190400000 to 1795194000000; 6 senders, 6 transfers, total 36000. T033368, T033403, T033439, T033474 and T033495 link to T033506 (A-20636 to A-36729, 30000). T033316 has no onward link. Max depth is 1 and the paths end at A-36729. A-36729's only later debit, T034128 at 1795200600000, is 7,800,000 ms after T033506 and is not linked. Path accounts: A-20636, A-36729. No shared device on its path.
None of the accounts on the alert paths other than the six alerted accounts has a fan-in alert. Within the dataset, no device used to send a contributing transfer was used by any other account.

What tells the alerts apart: as indicators the six are alike (5 to 8 distinct senders in one hour, one transfer per sender). The recorded relationships differ. (a) Onward links: A-28137 has none. A-85921 and A-20636 have one link each, to a single account, and some of their credits are unlinked. A-10859, A-37573 and A-83577 have multi-link paths of depth 3, 4 and 5, and every one of their contributing transfers starts a path. (b) Shared devices on the paths: A-37573's paths use one device, D-45880, across four of its five path accounts. A-10859's alerted account and first path account share D-79802. A-83577 has two non-adjacent path accounts on D-40018, which one outside account also used. A-85921, A-28137 and A-20636 have no shared device on their paths. (c) Amounts: A-85921 received six transfers of exactly 2500 each. A-37573's two path sequences repeat the same account order.

hypotheses.statement: A-37573 has deep, repeated onward-link sequences, and four of its path accounts sent from one device, D-45880. That fits the hypothesis that one party operates those accounts as a relay. The data does not establish ownership, control, or that the same funds moved. A shared device is consistent with other explanations too, such as a shared or institutional terminal or a data artefact.

A-10859 and A-83577 show the same pattern more weakly: a device shared by two path accounts (D-79802 and D-40018). For D-40018, the presence of the off-route account A-34114 could mean a shared or reused device rather than common control. Both readings are hypotheses only.

A-28137, A-85921 and A-20636 have no or shallow onward links and no shared devices on their paths. They could be benign aggregation, for example collections or a merchant-like receiver. The uniform 2500 amounts into A-85921 could be fixed-price payments or structured payments. The data does not say which, and these alerts should not be ranked as innocuous on that basis alone.
Ranking by recorded relationships alone, A-37573 looks the most worth reviewing, followed by A-83577 and A-10859. This is a triage suggestion, not a finding of fraud.

unresolved.question: Did the debits on the onward links actually carry the funds from the fan-in credits? Onward links record timing within 30 minutes only, so the data cannot answer this.

What happened to the accounts where the paths end (A-54215, A-10758, A-92332, A-85287, A-39382, A-36729, and A-28137 itself) outside this bounded dataset? The paths end only because no further qualifying transfer exists here.
Who uses devices D-45880, D-79802 and D-40018, and how is A-34114 related to the A-83577 path accounts, if at all? The data records device use, not identity or ownership.
Do the senders into each alerted account have any relationship beyond their single transfers? Nothing recorded here links them, and nothing outside the dataset is available.
